Hi Lena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete decision grid to help Edison pick two candidate models for a short evaluation run:

1) Goal recap
- Reduce latency on interactive search summaries to p50 < 120ms and p90 < 450ms for 256-token responses.
- Maintain human-evaluated relevance >= baseline (your in-house metric).
- Run a 48–72 hour throughput trial against a representative query mix.

2) Candidate prioritization (recommended order for pilot)
- Redwood-Opt-13B-q4 (best cost/latency tradeoff for conversational prompts)
- Mistral-22B-Instruct (higher quality for longer context; expect higher tail latency)
- Llama-2-70B-Chat (quality leader at higher cost; used as fallback where precision matters)

3) What I’m attaching / sharing
- decision-grid.xlsx (high-level prioritization and acceptance criteria) — attachment
- 2026-07-19_bench-snapshot.csv (short TPS & latency anchors from our lab runs) — attachment
- prompt-pack-v3.txt (seed prompts + regression guardrail prompts) — attachment
- Bench viewer (interactive): https://app.redwood.ai/bench/viewer?share=edison-4839

4) Test conditions we used for the anchors
- Sequence profile: median prompt 64 tokens, median generation 256 tokens.
- Concurrency: 16 streams, warm caches (KV warm).
- Hardware: 8xA100-80GB pool in us-west, optimized kernels.

Ask: If you can pick two models from the list above (one cost-efficient, one quality-first) we’ll stand up a short reserved trial and seed it with your sample prompt set. If procurement needs a summary of latency SLOs and expected cost, I’ll draft a one-page for them.

Thanks — Vivek

Hi Lena — good questions. Answers and a slightly expanded set of Redwood-verified anchors below.

Short answers:
- p90s in the attached snapshot were measured with KV cache warm (we run a warm-prefix profiling pass). Given your 60/40 repeating traffic, expect the effective p90 to track between our warm and cold numbers — typically ~1.2x the warm p90 depending on cache hit rate.
- Regression thresholds we recommend for pilot acceptance: human-evaluated relevance >= baseline - 3 points (on your 100-point scale) AND automated nDCG@10 drop <= 2.5%. Use the prompt-pack-v3 guardrail prompts for continuous checks.
- For the 48–72 hour trial we can guarantee reserved capacity at the requested TPS if you commit a short trial credit arrangement (standard internal paperwork) — I tailored three run profiles below.

Redwood-verified performance profiles (anchors) — measured at 256-gen / 64-prompt median, KV warm, 16 concurrent streams, us-west pool:
- Redwood-Opt-13B-q4: TPS (inference requests/sec) = 310, p50 latency = 95 ms, p90 latency = 360 ms
- Mistral-22B-Instruct: TPS = 140, p50 = 180 ms, p90 = 540 ms
- Llama-2-70B-Chat: TPS = 55, p50 = 320 ms, p90 = 920 ms

Notes on interpretation:
- TPS is observed end-to-end (network + runtime) for single-turn request patterns using our streaming path.
- Tail latency scales with concurrency and cold cache rate. If you expect many first-time prompts, plan for p90 ~ 1.5–2.0x our warm numbers for larger models.
- We recommend Redwood-Opt-13B-q4 as the cost-efficient anchor for interactive flows; Mistral-22B for a quality-first alt. Llama-2-70B is useful where you need highest quality for edge cases.

Quality/regression guardrails:
- Use prompt-pack-v3 guardrail prompts (attached) + a sampling plan: 2% of requests flagged for human review during the trial.
- If automated metrics show nDCG@10 drop > 2.5% OR human drift > 3 points on 100-point scale, trigger a rollback to the baseline model and open an investigation ticket.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You pick two models (cost + quality).
2) We provision a 72-hour reserved trial with the profile you pick.
3) Redwood runs the trial and shares a report (bench viewer link + csv) and a short one-pager for procurement that summarizes expected monthly cost at projected QPS.

I’ve attached the lab snapshot and the prompt pack. If you want, I can also send a compact one-page SLA summary for procurement to speed sign-off.

Cheers,
Vivek
